# Compatibility

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-feature-docs.mjs from the data; edit the data, then run it again. -->

The devices, services, browsers and systems Dayspring works with, and how sure we are. Settings → This app → **Compatibility** has the same list, searchable, with the setup steps for each one.

- ✅ **Verified:** confirmed on a real device by the owner.
- 🧪 **Passes simulator tests:** Dayspring's automated tests pass against a simulated device of this kind.
- 👍 **Expected to work:** it uses a protocol Dayspring speaks, according to the maker's or the community's documentation.
- ❔ **Untested:** it might work; nobody has tried it yet.
- ⛔ **Not supported:** it can't work with Dayspring (the reason is given).

**Works offline** means it keeps working with no internet once it's set up.

## Power strips and plugs

Smart power strips, plugs and relays that switch things on and off, plus the other ways Dayspring can power a device: waking a computer over the network and turning a TV on or to standby over HDMI. The recommended ones work on your home network with no internet.

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TP-Link Kasa HS300 smart power strip (6 outlets)** | 🧪 tested-sim | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, per-outlet, power-monitoring, schedules | Recommended. Six outlets, each switched on its own and each with its own power reading (watts), so Dayspring can answer "what's drawing power?". The three USB ports are always on. Dayspring talks to it directly on your network with Kasa's local protocol; no cloud is used. Newer hardware versions may ask for your TP-Link login once. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Kasa's local protocol, each outlet. Not yet tried on a real one. |
| **TP-Link Kasa KP303 smart power strip (3 outlets)** | 🧪 tested-sim | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, per-outlet, schedules | Three switchable outlets plus two always-on USB ports. No power readings. Controlled directly by Dayspring with Kasa's local protocol. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Kasa's local protocol, each outlet. Not yet tried on a real one. |
| **TP-Link Kasa KP400 / EP40 outdoor smart plug (2 outlets)** | 👍 expected | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, per-outlet, schedules | Weather-resistant plug with two outlets switched separately, for outdoor lights, fountains or holiday lights. No power readings. The EP40 is the newer version of the same idea. Works directly with Dayspring on your network. |
| **TP-Link Kasa EP10 / HS103 mini smart plug** | 👍 expected | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, schedules | A single-outlet plug, handy for a lamp or a fan. No power readings (the KP115 and EP25 plugs add them). Works directly with Dayspring on your network. |
| **TP-Link Kasa KP125M smart plug (Matter, energy monitoring)** | 🧪 tested-sim | Matter / Thread via Home Assistant | yes | on-off, power-monitoring, schedules | A Matter plug with power readings. The most reliable way is Matter through Home Assistant. It uses TP-Link's newer login-checked local protocol rather than the classic Kasa one, so adding it directly as a Kasa device needs your TP-Link login and may not work on every firmware. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Added directly as a Kasa device with your TP-Link login, over TP-Link's newer KLAP local protocol. Not yet tried on a real one. |

Home Assistant's community local Tuya integrations do this today; Dayspring's own local Tuya support is planned. Firmware updates can sometimes change the key. |

## Bulbs and lights

Smart bulbs, lamps, dimmers and light hubs. Dayspring talks to a Hue bridge directly; most other lights come in through Home Assistant, which controls them on your own network.

| **Philips Hue Hue Bridge with any Hue bulbs, lamps or fixtures** | 🧪 tested-sim | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, brightness, color, color-temperature, scenes | Recommended. Dayspring talks to the bridge's local API directly; the bridge talks to the bulbs over Zigbee. No cloud is needed once paired. White-only bulbs support brightness (and warmth for White Ambiance). Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): The Hue bridge's local API. Not yet tried on a real one. |
| **Philips Hue Hue bulbs used with Bluetooth only (no bridge)** | ⛔ not-supported | Bluetooth LE | yes | on-off, brightness, color, color-temperature | Not supported: Without a bridge, Hue bulbs are controlled only by the Hue phone app over Bluetooth, which has no documented protocol for computers. ## LED strips

LED strips and their controllers: colour, brightness, effects and segments. WLED is the recommended choice and Dayspring talks to it directly; Bluetooth-only strips are coming through this PC's Bluetooth or ESPHome Bluetooth proxies.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **WLED (open firmware) ESP32 / ESP8266 LED controllers running WLED** | 🧪 tested-sim | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, brightness, color, effects, segments, music-sync, scenes | Recommended. WLED is free firmware for small Wi-Fi LED controllers that drive addressable strips (WS2812B, SK6812 and similar). Dayspring talks to it directly on your network: no account, no cloud, over a hundred built-in effects, and presets you save in WLED. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): WLED's own local controls. Not yet tried on a real one. |

Once on your Wi-Fi they work exactly like the WLED entry. |

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ESPHome (open firmware) ESP32 Bluetooth proxy** | 👍 expected | Bluetooth LE | yes | sensor | Recommended in the home-control plan. A cheap ESP32 board on your Wi-Fi (or wired network) that listens for and talks to Bluetooth devices nearby, extending Bluetooth range to every room. Home Assistant uses them automatically; Dayspring will use them for its own Bluetooth control too. |
| **SwitchBot Bot (button pusher)** | 👍 expected | Bluetooth LE | yes | on-off, battery | A small arm that presses a physical button or rocker switch, handy for a coffee maker or an old appliance. | **Ruuvi RuuviTag environmental sensor** | 👍 expected | Bluetooth LE | yes | sensor, temperature, humidity, battery | A rugged sensor (temperature, humidity, air pressure, movement) with an open Bluetooth format, read by Home Assistant's RuuviTag integration. Good for a shop, garage or outdoors. |

## 3D printers

3D printers Dayspring can watch and control on the home network or over USB: status, camera, temperatures, pause, resume, cancel and starting a print. Starting a print always needs the owner's yes and a bed-clear check first, because a printer heats up and moves.

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bambu Lab X1 Carbon** | 🧪 tested-sim | Home network (local) | yes | status, camera, temperatures, pause, resume, cancel, start-print, upload, light, speed, ams | Talks to the printer itself in LAN mode: status and commands over the printer's own MQTT (encrypted, port 8883, user bblp and the access code), files over FTPS (port 990), and the camera as an RTSPS stream (port 322). The Bambu account and cloud are never used. Since 2025, Bambu's firmware (X1 01.08.03 and newer) only accepts control commands from other software when LAN Only Mode AND Developer Mode are both on; without them, status still arrives but pause and start are ignored, and Dayspring says so. Safety: starting a print always needs the owner's yes and a bed-clear check with the camera (heat and motion). Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Status and the camera, and the clear message when Developer Mode is off and the printer refuses commands. Not yet tried on a real one. |

## Cameras

Cameras Dayspring can show and watch: USB webcams, security cameras on the home network (RTSP, ONVIF, snapshot addresses), GoPros, 3D printer cameras, cameras from Home Assistant, and trail cameras whose photos arrive by email or in a folder. Camera passwords are stored encrypted with Windows.

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |

Pictures never leave the computer unless AI analysis is turned on for that camera. Only one app can use a webcam at a time, so a video call may take it over. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): The capture settings Dayspring gives ffmpeg (DirectShow). Not yet tried on a real one. |

RTSP and ONVIF are off by default on newer firmware. Newer 4K models use the H.265 stream address. Everything stays on the home network. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Reolink's snapshot address. Not yet tried on a real one. |

## Smart-home hubs and bridges

Hubs, bridges and radio sticks that connect many devices at once. Home Assistant is the recommended backbone: it runs Zigbee, Z-Wave, Thread/Matter and thousands of integrations on your own network, and Dayspring controls anything it runs.

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Home Assistant Home Assistant (OS, Green, Yellow or a mini PC)** | 🧪 tested-sim | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, brightness, color, color-temperature, effects, open-close, lock, temperature, sensor, scenes | Recommended backbone. Dayspring connects to Home Assistant's REST and WebSocket APIs with a long-lived access token and can then control its lights, switches, covers, locks, thermostats, fans and media players. Everything stays on your network. The most important devices (strips, LED controllers, printers) also connect to Dayspring directly, so they keep working if Home Assistant is down. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Home Assistant's API. Not yet tried on a real one. |
| **Hubitat Hubitat Elevation hub (Maker API)** | ❔ untested | Home network (local) | yes | on-off | Hubitat runs locally and its Maker API app gives each device simple web addresses for on and off. Dayspring's custom web-request device can call those, so on/off should work; it hasn't been tried. For more than on and off, Hubitat can share devices with Home Assistant. |
| **Samsung SmartThings (hub or app)** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | on-off, brightness, color, sensor, lock | SmartThings is reached through Samsung's cloud, so it needs the internet. Home Assistant's SmartThings integration brings its devices in, and Dayspring controls them from there. Over time, prefer moving important devices to a local connection. |
| **SONOFF ZBDongle-E (Zigbee 3.0 USB Dongle Plus, EFR32)** | 👍 expected | Zigbee via Home Assistant | yes | sensor | A low-cost USB Zigbee coordinator for Home Assistant (ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT). Once it's set up, every Zigbee bulb, sensor and plug you pair shows up in Dayspring through Home Assistant. |
| **SONOFF ZBDongle-P (Zigbee 3.0 USB Dongle Plus, CC2652P)** | 👍 expected | Zigbee via Home Assistant | yes | sensor | The Texas Instruments–based version of SONOFF's Zigbee stick; well supported by both ZHA and Zigbee2MQTT. |
| **Home Assistant Home Assistant Connect ZBT-1 (Zigbee or Thread)** | 👍 expected | Zigbee via Home Assistant | yes | sensor | Home Assistant's own USB stick. It runs Zigbee, or Thread for Matter-over-Thread devices, and Home Assistant sets it up almost automatically. Using one stick for both at once is experimental; many homes use one stick per radio. |
| **Zooz ZST39 800 Series Z-Wave Long Range USB stick** | 👍 expected | Z-Wave via Home Assistant | yes | sensor | A Z-Wave coordinator for Home Assistant (Z-Wave JS). Z-Wave is common for locks, in-wall switches and sensors, and Long Range reaches detached garages and sheds. |
| **Matter / Thread Matter and Thread devices via Home Assistant** | 🧪 tested-sim | Matter / Thread via Home Assistant | yes | on-off, brightness, color, color-temperature, open-close, lock, sensor | Matter is the cross-brand standard; Thread is the low-power radio many Matter devices use. Home Assistant is a Matter controller (Wi-Fi and Thread) and can share devices already set up in Apple, Google or Amazon homes. Thread devices need a Thread border router (a ZBT-1 or a compatible speaker or hub). Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Matter devices through Home Assistant. Not yet tried on a real one. |
| **Bond Bond Bridge (ceiling fans, shades, fireplaces)** | 👍 expected | Home network (local) | yes | on-off, brightness, open-close, ir-learn | Learns the radio (RF) and infrared remotes of ceiling fans, shades and fireplaces and controls them from your network. It has a local API used by Home Assistant's Bond integration. Fireplaces are heat devices and shades are motion devices: Dayspring's safety rules apply. |
| **Broadlink RM4 Mini / RM4 Pro (IR and RF blaster)** | 👍 expected | Infrared | yes | ir-learn, on-off | Learns the buttons of infrared remotes (older TVs, fans, AC units, soundbars; the Pro also does some RF remotes) and sends them locally. Home Assistant's Broadlink integration learns and sends commands today; Dayspring's own infrared support is planned. IR is one-way, so Dayspring can't tell whether the device actually changed. |
| **ratgdo ratgdo garage door controller** | 👍 expected | Home network (local) | yes | open-close, sensor, on-off | Stage 3. A small board wired to your garage door opener that controls it locally and reports whether the door is open, with no cloud. It runs ESPHome (or MQTT firmware) and shows up in Home Assistant. A garage door is a motion device: Dayspring asks for confirmation, never includes it in "turn everything on", and can alert if it's left open. |
| **SwitchBot Hub 2** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | temperature, humidity, ir-learn, sensor | Connects SwitchBot Bluetooth devices to SwitchBot's cloud, learns IR remotes and has its own temperature sensor. Newer firmware can also share devices over Matter. |

It publishes each device over MQTT, so Dayspring can switch plugs and relays with its Zigbee2MQTT template even without Home Assistant, or through Home Assistant for everything else. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Zigbee2MQTT over MQTT. Not yet tried on a real one. |

Prefer local Tuya control (see the Tuya plug, bulb and strip entries) for anything important. |

## Email providers

Mailboxes Dayspring can read, organise and (with your yes) send from: Gmail and Outlook through their own sign-in, and most other providers through IMAP and SMTP with an app password. Passwords are stored encrypted with Windows, and nothing is ever sent without the owner's yes.

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Google Gmail** | 🧪 tested-sim | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, labels, attachments | Best through Google sign-in: Dayspring uses the Gmail API with the Google account connection, asking for reading first and for sending or organising only when you turn those on. IMAP with a Google app password (two-step verification on) also works. The email test script runs every step against a stand-in Gmail server. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Gmail, against stand-ins (mocks). Not yet tried on a real one. |
| **Microsoft Outlook.com / Hotmail / Live** | 🧪 tested-sim | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | Through Microsoft sign-in and Microsoft Graph: reading, drafts, marking and moving, and sending only after you turn it on. Microsoft now prefers this over passwords for Outlook.com. The email test script runs it against a stand-in Microsoft Graph. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): Outlook, against stand-ins (mocks). Not yet tried on a real one. |
| **Microsoft Microsoft 365 work or school mailbox** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | Uses the same Microsoft sign-in and Graph connection as Outlook.com. Many organisations only let approved apps in, so your IT admin may need to allow Dayspring (admin consent) before you can sign in. |
| **Yahoo Yahoo Mail** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | IMAP (imap.mail.yahoo.com, port 993) and SMTP (smtp.mail.yahoo.com, port 465). Yahoo needs an app password; your normal password won't work. Dayspring fills in the servers when you type a Yahoo address. |
| **Apple iCloud Mail** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | IMAP (imap.mail.me.com, port 993) and SMTP (smtp.mail.me.com, port 587). Apple needs two-factor authentication on and an app-specific password. |
| **AOL AOL Mail** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | IMAP (imap.aol.com, port 993) and SMTP (smtp.aol.com, port 465) with an app password. |
| **Zoho Zoho Mail** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | IMAP (imap.zoho.com) and SMTP (smtp.zoho.com). IMAP access must be turned on in Zoho first, and with two-factor on you need an app-specific password. Accounts in other regions use that region's servers (for example imap.zoho.eu or imap.zoho.in); type them in by hand if yours is one of those. |
| **GMX GMX Mail** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | IMAP (imap.gmx.com, port 993) and SMTP (mail.gmx.com, port 587). Access for other apps must be allowed in GMX webmail first. Your GMX password works, or an app password if two-factor is on. |
| **Fastmail Fastmail** | 👍 expected | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | IMAP (imap.fastmail.com, port 993) and SMTP (smtp.fastmail.com, port 465) with an app password that has IMAP and SMTP access. |
| **Proton Proton Mail** | ❔ untested | Internet service | no | read, search, send | Proton Mail is end-to-end encrypted and has no ordinary IMAP server. Other apps can only reach it through Proton Mail Bridge, a program that runs on this computer and is available on paid Proton plans. Bridge gives local IMAP and SMTP addresses and its own password, which Dayspring should be able to use like any IMAP account; this hasn't been tried. |
| **Any Any provider with IMAP and SMTP** | 🧪 tested-sim | Internet service | no | read, search, drafts, send, organize, folders, attachments | Most email providers offer IMAP for reading and SMTP for sending. Passes Dayspring's simulator tests (September 2026): IMAP and SMTP, against stand-ins (mocks). Not yet tried on a real one. |

## GIF providers

Where Dayspring's GIF picker finds GIFs and stickers. The web search works with no key at all; free keys from GIPHY or KLIPY add much bigger libraries. All sources are searched at once and mixed into one list.

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GIPHY GIPHY API** | 🧪 tested-sim | Internet service | no | search, trending, categories, stickers, ratings | The biggest GIF library. A free beta key allows about 100 searches an hour, which is plenty for one home. Results are shown with "Powered by GIPHY", as GIPHY asks. The GIF test script checks it against a stand-in GIPHY server. |
| **KLIPY KLIPY API** | 🧪 tested-sim | Internet service | no | search, trending, categories, stickers, ratings | A large free GIF, sticker and meme library, and the usual replacement for Tenor. Results are shown with "Powered by KLIPY". Dayspring never asks for ads. The GIF test script checks it against a stand-in KLIPY server. |
| **Imgur Imgur API** | 🧪 tested-sim | Internet service | no | search, trending | Animated GIFs from Imgur's gallery, with a free Client ID. Imgur doesn't rate its content, so it's only used when the rating setting is PG-13 or R. No stickers. The GIF test script checks it against a stand-in Imgur server. |
| **Web Web image search (keyless)** | 🧪 tested-sim | Internet service | no | search, trending, stickers, safe-search | Animated pictures from the web image search (DuckDuckGo, then Bing) with their animated-GIF filter. No account and no key, so GIFs always work, and it steps in when every other source is busy. The web isn't rated, so SafeSearch does the filtering. The GIF test script checks it with no keys at all against a stand-in search. |
| **Google Tenor API** | ⛔ not-supported | Internet service | no |  | Not supported: Google shut down the Tenor API for good on June 30, 2026, and took no new keys from January 2026. |

Dayspring opens it with its own profile as an app window, full screen on a TV, or the mini window. ## Operating systems

Dayspring runs on Windows: its helpers (the window, the overlay, sounds, keep-awake, reading text on screen, encrypted passwords) use Windows' own parts. It needs Node.js 22.13 or newer, which comes with the installer.

| Device | Status | Connection | Works offline | Can do | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Microsoft Windows 11 (23H2, 24H2, 25H2)** | ✅ verified | On this computer | yes | full-app, dpapi, powershell-5-1, whisper, overlay, keep-awake | In the owner's daily use (September 2026): Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200). 23H2 and 24H2 use the same parts and should behave the same. Home and Pro both work. |
| **Microsoft Windows 10 (1809 and newer, best on 22H2)** | 🧪 tested-sim | On this computer | yes | full-app, dpapi, powershell-5-1, whisper, overlay, keep-awake | Dayspring works on Windows 10. A test script checks that every PowerShell script runs in Windows PowerShell 5.1, every C# helper builds with the .NET Framework compiler that comes with Windows 10, no Windows 11-only features are used, and only Windows' own tar is used. Microsoft ended free support for Windows 10 on October 14, 2025, so it no longer gets security updates unless enrolled in Extended Security Updates; Dayspring still runs, but upgrading to Windows 11 is wise. |
| **Microsoft Windows 10 versions before 1803** | ⛔ not-supported | On this computer | yes |  | Not supported: These early Windows 10 versions lack the built-in tar that Dayspring's installer and updates use, and are older than what Dayspring is checked against (1809 and newer). Windows 8.1, 7 and older can't run Node.js 22.13 at all. |
| **Microsoft Windows 11 on Arm (Snapdragon PCs)** | ❔ untested | On this computer | yes |  | Node.js has Arm builds for Windows, and Windows on Arm can also run x64 programs through emulation. Parts Dayspring ships as x64 programs (ffmpeg, the whisper speech recognition) would run emulated and may be slower. Not tried. |
| **Microsoft Windows Server 2019 / 2022 / 2025** | ❔ untested | On this computer | yes |  | Shares most parts with Windows 10 and 11, but servers often lack desktop audio, a microphone and some desktop features, and are locked down more. Not tried. |
| **Apple macOS** | ⛔ not-supported | On this computer | yes |  | Not supported: Dayspring's helpers are Windows-only: PowerShell scripts, C# helpers for the window and overlay, Windows audio, Windows DPAPI for encrypted passwords, and Windows OCR. |
| **Linux Linux distributions** | ⛔ not-supported | On this computer | yes |  | Not supported: Dayspring's helpers are Windows-only (PowerShell, C# helpers, Windows audio, DPAPI encryption, Windows OCR). |
